trace_steps: frame_retriever returns frame_18.50.png at 18.5s as the representative shirt view (relevance_score 0.6687), so I use that frame as the answer-critical visual anchor.

In frame_18.50.png at 18.5s, spatial_grounder reports the standard shirt openings: a neck opening at bbox [420, 41, 578, 148] (confidence 0.98), a left sleeve opening at [295, 220, 385, 340] (confidence 0.97), a right sleeve opening at [630, 220, 715, 340] (confidence 0.97), and a bottom opening at [358, 810, 638, 880] (confidence 0.99).

The same spatial_grounder result on frame_18.50.png also reports two additional fabric tears: a left-side tear at [425, 405, 500, 655] (confidence 0.96) and a right-side tear at [510, 590, 570, 800] (confidence 0.95). Its spatial description says the T-shirt has the four standard openings plus two distinct tears on the torso.
Counting the visible holes from that grounded evidence gives 4 standard openings + 2 tears = 6 holes.
Therefore the correct option is E. 6.
